title: Intersection with an ideal generated by a regular sequence modulo another ideal
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I$ an ideal of $R$, and $g_1,\dots,g_m\in R$ elements whose images in $R/I$ form a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Put $K=(g_1,\dots,g_m)\subseteq R$. Then $I\cap K=IK$ as ideals of $R$.

proof.text: Apply the split auxiliary inclusion `aux-regular-quotient-ideal-intersection-inclusion` to obtain I ⊓ Ideal.ofList gs ≤ I * Ideal.ofList gs. For the reverse inclusion, use that ideal multiplication is contained in each factor, then conclude by antisymmetry.
